reasons: 1 of 1 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — a 3-turnover swing — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a away margin of 9 and the game finished 24 the away way — 15 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 3-turnover swing
variance_markers.text: Missouri Tigers won the turnover battle by 3. Turnover margin is the least repeatable thing in football: it moves scoreboards hard and predicts almost nothing about the next meeting, so a result built on it says less about either team than the scoreline suggests.

variance_markers.label: A 24-point margin
variance_markers.text: Once a game is this far apart both teams stop playing the game they were rated on — the leader runs clock, the trailer throws — so late-game rates describe the situation rather than either team.

variance_markers.label: 1 non-offensive or return score
variance_markers.text: Points that arrived without an offensive drive. They count the same on the scoreboard and belong to a different distribution from the one the model prices.

verdict.line: No sportsbook quote was captured before publication, so there is no bet result to separate from the process. The reasoning is graded on its own below, which is the half that compounds.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: Arkansas holds the largest measured edge in this matchup: Arkansas 49.1 (#66 of 138) vs Missouri 41.7 (#108 of 138) — 42 places on the national board.

lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Arkansas as better in rushing and the game went the other way. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 10.5 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 8 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, matchup.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.
